result.title: OPDArena: Understanding Learning and Forgetting in On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly used for language model post-training, yet how teacher supervision shapes learning and forgetting remains unclear. We present OPDArena, a framework comparing supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and OPD across five pretrained models and diverse teacher sources. It jointly evaluates mathematical learning, general capability retention, and predictive distribution changes. Teacher choice strongly shapes retention: students of RLVR-trained teachers improve on the target task while retaining prior capabilities, whereas students of SFT-trained teachers incur greater capability loss. Across post-training methods, out-of-domain (OOD) distribution change shows a more consistent positive association with forgetting than in-domain change. To understand how teacher choice affects these changes, we examine the additional information teachers provide relative to the student's pretrained model. Controlled teacher comparisons show that the task-specific preferences teachers acquire through post-training make student updates more concentrated in-domain.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 OPDArena 框架，在五个预训练模型与多种教师来源上对比 SFT、RLVR 与 on-policy distillation，联合评估目标任务学习、通用能力保持和预测分布变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用「教师相对学生预训练模型的额外信息」解释更新集中度，并区分域内/域外分布变化与遗忘，可能为 latent 推理轨迹训练中的监督信号贡献分配与状态分布漂移诊断提供可核查的方法线索，但本文仅涉及纯文本后训练，需人工判断迁移价值。
